title: AID plan-lifecycle manifest (IMP-232 v2.58.0)
description: Git-tracked, PUBLIC-SAFE durable denominator + structured deps + delivery provenance for a plan. Technical receipt fields only — no report bodies, findings, prompts, absolute paths, secrets, PII, or waiver reasons.

mode.description: P064 E-064-1_2 Step 3: the authoritative release model for this plan. Absent on a manifest created before P064 (or by ensure_manifest without an explicit mode write) — absence means legacy_epic_release_mode (aid_lifecycle_plan_mode's documented default), never a hard failure. Written durably by aid_lifecycle_set_plan_mode (lib/aid-lifecycle.sh) so a hand-edited/deleted runtime plan-state.yaml can never silently change which model a plan follows.

scope.description: P068 E-068-1_2 Step 5 (CF1) widens this from [required, backlog]. `abandoned` and `superseded` are written by plan-merge-to-main, in the SAME commit as the delivery bindings, for EPICs the PM terminated without delivery — so aid_plan_closure_state stops counting them in the required denominator and the plan can close. They are NOT written at epic-complete: _aid_lc_require_target_branch refuses a lifecycle write off the target branch, and epic-complete runs on a task branch. The PM's REASON deliberately does not live here — this file is additionalProperties:false and aid_lifecycle_publicsafe_check rejects a free-text `reason` key; the reason is recorded in the runtime plan-state and the operation log.

status.description: P068 E-068-1_2 Step 5: the plan's terminal lifecycle status, durable on the target branch. Absent means `active` (every manifest written before P068). Step 6 (plan-close) owns the transition to `closed`; an aborted plan is recorded as `aborted`; a plan that merged and was then reverted is `rolled_back` (P075 dogfood, 2026-07-27) — neither `aborted`, which would deny the merge, nor `closed`, which would claim a delivery no longer on the target branch. Deliberately additive: the receipt remains the authoritative closure artifact, this is the manifest-side flag closure predicates can read without resolving a second file.

rollback.description: The durable, git-tracked rollback record. It exists because the runtime marker under .aid-o/ is gitignored: without this block a fresh clone would read `deliveries` and conclude the plan was delivered, while the local workspace said it had been rolled back. Two truths, which is exactly what the plan boundary removes. Free-text is excluded on purpose — publicsafe_check forbids a `reason` key in a tracked artifact, and the human reason belongs in the runtime marker and the operation log.

candidate_sha.description: The candidate the PM approved and that was merged.

target_head_before_merge.description: The target-branch head the candidate was approved against — what the revert restored the branch to.

merge_commit.description: The published plan merge. Must remain reachable: a rollback is a revert forward, never a rewrite.

revert_commit.description: The commit that restored the pre-merge content. Verified by comparing ITS tree against the pre-merge tree outside .aid-lifecycle/, not merely by ancestry.

decision_ref.description: A technical reference to where the human reason lives (an op-log id or the runtime marker path). The reason itself is deliberately NOT here: this manifest is git-tracked and public-safe, and the contract forbids free-text keys.
